title: Axis Cascade initiative matrix and exec update (v0.1)
content:
PURPOSE
This is a working draft that introduces the Axis Cascade method for stitching quarterly initiatives to a single executive narrative and the all-company comms for the next 90→180 day window.

High-level goal: Rapidly align the leadership cohort on three cross-cutting initiatives that materially change our inference unit economics and customer reliability story. Use this doc as a lightweight decision matrix plus the exec talking points for the leadership update.

PRINCIPLES (quick)
- Single narrative: choose one coherent frame per quarter rather than many unconnected asks.
- Outcome-first OKRs: start from measurable customer/monetary outcomes, then map initiatives.
- Risk-prioritize: surface failure modes early, set contingency triggers.
- Lightweight comms: single page for execs + 3 talking bullets for each manager.

AXIS CASCADE OVERVIEW (how it works)
1) Axis = primary company objective (North Star for the cycle).
2) Cascade = three initiative lanes (Infra, Product, Go-to-Market) that each get 1–2 focused KR candidates.
3) Decision matrix: trade-offs and fallback policies are recorded against each KR (cost impact, latency delta, rollout complexity).

Current candidate Axis (for Q2→Q3 cycle): "Make inference 3x cheaper at p95 latency target for hosted API customers."
Why: clear unit-economics lift, aligns product demand and infra work, sells well to customers at enterprise renewal time.

CANDIDATE OKRs (raw, for debate)
O: Improve hosted inference economics while preserving p95 latency SLOs
KR1: Reduce per-token GPU seconds by 60% for median request through batching + KV prefix caching improvements (measure: GPU-seconds/1k tokens).
KR2: Deliver two quantized model profiles validated for parity on priority prompt-suite (quality delta < 3% on regression metric).
KR3: Achieve 99.9% uptime for hosted-model endpoints under 24/7 traffic pattern for a 30-day window.

Cascade lanes (initiative mapping):
- Infra lane (owner: Ravi Singh): Continuous batching engine (v2), auto-bump grouping, cold-start KV cache prewarm. Linked ticket: ENG-7362.
  - Key actions: prototype grouping heuristic (2 sprints), telemetry gates, rollout canary to 5% traffic.
  - Risk: regression in tail latency if batch windows misestimate short requests. Contingency: dynamic cutoff and immediate rollback to v1.

- Product lane (owner: Eleni Park): Prompt-set driven quantization profiles + catalog flags (2 profiles: quality-first, cost-first).
  - Key actions: eval harness, integration tests with streaming. GH PR: redwood-inference/platform#1824.
  - Risk: customer-visible hallucination increase. Contingency: phased opt-in + default fallback to FP16.

- GTM + CS lane (owner: Tomás Rivera): Customer pilots for pricing experiments and renewal playbook.
  - Key actions: 6 pilot customers for early adopter program, playbook for solutions engineers.
  - Risk: slow uptake. Contingency: expand incentives, shorten pilot.

COMMUNICATIONS AND TIMELINE (exec update + company touch)
- Week 0 (leadership sync): present Axis + decision matrix, ask execs to commit owners and accept tradeoffs.
- Week 1–4 (build): infra & product sprint zero; GTM lines prepping pilot cohort.
- Week 5 (mid-sprint review): technical demo + canary plan for infra.
- Week 8 (leadership checkpoint): go/no-go on broad rollout, prepare exec update for the company.
- Week 9 (company-wide comms): single-slide narrative + three manager bullets + FAQ doc.

Exec update talking points (3 mins)
- What: We chose an "economics-first" axis to improve hosted API unit costs while keeping latency and quality stable.
- So what: If successful, this lowers hosting price pressure and shortens time-to-value for customers; enables competitive pricing.
- Ask: Approve the Axis, the three lane owners, and the pre-approved rollback triggers.

Company comms slip (manager bullets)
(Managers get three quick bullets to explain to their teams)
- Bullet 1: Why - this reduces our cost per inference and helps us be more competitive.
- Bullet 2: What - engineering and product are focusing on batching, KV cache, and quantized profiles; expect early pilots.
- Bullet 3: What I need from you - fast feedback on regressions, help with test harnesses and pilot engagement.

FAQ (short)
Q: Are we changing pricing now?
A: No — pilots first. Pricing changes would happen after verified rollback-safe gains and a 30-day stability window.

Q: Does this impact Dedicated/Private customers?
A: Dedicated gets the same runtime improvements; Private packages will be offered as opt-in with migration guides.

RISKS, OPEN QUESTIONS, DECISIONS NEEDED
- Risk: Quality regressions detectable only in long-tail prompts. Decision: expand eval set by 30% before canary. (Owner: Eleni)
- Question: Are we comfortable with a 5% canary for infra given SLOs? (Need signoff from SRE/Platform)
- Decision: Pre-approve a fallback to FP16 runtime if quantized profile fails QA. (Proposed by Product)

NEXT STEPS & ACTIONS (short checklist)
- [ ] Leadership commit (this meeting): accept Axis and owners (assigned).
- [ ] Engineering: define telemetry gates + ENG-7362 scope (Ravi) — due Week 1.
- [ ] Product: finalize eval harness with 3 regression suites (Eleni) — due Week 2.
- [ ] GTM: identify 6 pilot customers + draft pilot incentive (Tomás) — due Week 3.
- [ ] Comms: one-slide narrative + manager bullets + FAQ (Maya) — due Week 8.

NOTES TO SELF (working)
- Keep this doc intentionally concise — full PRD lives in Confluence link in linked_artifacts.
- We should add cost modeling appendix if leadership asks for $/token impact.
- Capture one fallback scenario that maps to RBAC changes for Dedicated customers.

ANNOTATIONS / REFERENCES
- See ENG-7362 for infra backlog lines and perf telemetry.
- GH PR redwood-inference/platform#1824 contains product integration notes and unit tests.
- Confluence page AXIS-2026 contains the long-form PRD, data tables, and evaluation results.

END (v0.1) — feedback welcome in the thread or directly edit.
